items.title: Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability
items.summary_1line: Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment. By Craig Risi
items.editor_note: 유일한 프로덕션 사례로, Netflix는 AI 에이전트들이 운영에 대한 모델을 공유하도록 온톨로지 기반 지식 그래프를 구축한다.

items.title: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding
items.summary_1line: Introduces PoVi, a benchmark and agentic framework that turns poems into narrated videos via knowledge-grounded planning, reporting gains over single-call generation across three planners and four video generators.

items.title: Show HN: Dev-Mem – Local-first SQLite knowledge graph for AI coding agents
items.summary_1line: Dev-Mem is a local-first tool that gives AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode a persistent SQLite knowledge store of decisions, failed approaches and constraints, injected into new sessions and optionally shared via Git.
items.editor_note: 최신 항목: Dev-Mem은 코딩 에이전트에 의사결정과 실패한 접근법을 저장하는 로컬 SQLite 저장소를 제공하며, 선택적으로 Git으로 공유할 수 있다.

editorial.tldr: This thread has been narrowed from a 77-item "large language" bucket to 8 items about knowledge engineering: LLM agents that build taxonomies, ontologies and knowledge graphs. It is a research theme, not one event: arXiv papers on agent-built knowledge bases ran alongside Netflix's Nov 13 production knowledge graph for observability agents.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 26: Dev-Mem, a Show HN tool, gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode a local SQLite store of past decisions, failed approaches and constraints, injected into each new session and optionally shared via Git.
editorial.why_it_matters: Agent context is moving from retrieved chunks to curated, structured knowledge (ontologies, graphs, decision logs), so platform teams now own a knowledge base that needs schema, freshness and review like any other data store.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you give coding agents a persistent memory store such as Dev-Mem, review entries like code: it is injected into every session, so a stale "failed approach" or wrong constraint will steer each future run until someone deletes it.

beats.headline: Papers put LLM agents to work building taxonomies, hypergraphs and ontologies
beats.summary: Agent-built knowledge bases are framed as the step past chunk and graph RAG, and gained a task-grounded benchmark on Nov 20.

beats.headline: Netflix turns operational data into a knowledge graph for its AI agents
beats.summary: The one production case: an ontology gives investigation agents a shared model of Netflix's environment.

beats.headline: Stored knowledge feeds eval rubrics and grounded generation
beats.summary: Past evaluation cases become rubrics for LLM judges, and knowledge grounding guides an agentic poem-to-video pipeline.

beats.headline: Dev-Mem gives coding agents a local decision memory

open_questions: Does persistent agent memory like Dev-Mem get a measured effect on coding-agent task success, not just a demo?
Does Netflix publish numbers on how much its knowledge graph shortens production investigations?
Which agents and models score best on AutoOntologyBench, and does any team adopt it as a regression eval?
How do shared agent knowledge stores handle stale or contradicted entries once several engineers commit to them via Git?
